content.text: Field teams often {{gap:1}} careful notes before they {{gap:2}} a conclusion. This habit can {{gap:3}} researchers from making a hasty {{gap:4}} and helps them {{gap:5}} patterns that would otherwise {{gap:6}} unnoticed. A clear record also {{gap:7}} later comparison and {{gap:8}} shared discussion.

questions.explanation: The established collocation is take notes.

distractorExplanations.A: Make notes is possible in some varieties, but take notes is the intended collocation here.
distractorExplanations.C: Do notes is not idiomatic English.
distractorExplanations.D: Set notes does not fit this meaning.

questions.explanation: Reach a conclusion is the standard collocation.

distractorExplanations.A: Draw a conclusion can be valid, but does not fit the chosen intended phrasing.
distractorExplanations.B: Pull a conclusion is not idiomatic.
distractorExplanations.D: Touch a conclusion does not express making a judgement.

questions.explanation: Prevent someone from doing something fits the grammar and meaning.

distractorExplanations.B: Avoid does not take the structure researchers from making.
distractorExplanations.C: Refuse would require a different subject and construction.
distractorExplanations.D: Deny does not mean stop someone from acting.

questions.explanation: Make a hasty judgement is the intended collocation.

distractorExplanations.A: Make a hasty decision is possible, but the context concerns interpretation rather than action.
distractorExplanations.B: Choice does not collocate as naturally with hasty here.
distractorExplanations.C: Conclusion repeats the idea already expressed by the following gap.

questions.explanation: Notice patterns is the natural verb choice here.

distractorExplanations.B: Observe patterns is possible, but is less precise for patterns discovered incidentally.
distractorExplanations.C: Watch normally describes sustained visual attention.
distractorExplanations.D: Look requires a suitable particle or preposition in this structure.

questions.explanation: Remain unnoticed expresses the intended state.

distractorExplanations.B: Stay unnoticed is possible but less formal than the intended choice.
distractorExplanations.C: Go unnoticed describes escaping attention, not a continuing state in this passage.
distractorExplanations.D: Pass unnoticed does not fit the plural subject and meaning as well.

questions.explanation: Enables later comparison is the best formal collocation.

distractorExplanations.A: Allows is grammatical, but less precise in this formal context.
distractorExplanations.B: Permits usually suggests permission rather than making an activity possible.
distractorExplanations.D: Lets is too informal and would normally be followed by an object before the verb.

questions.explanation: Supports shared discussion fits the meaning.

distractorExplanations.B: Hold discussion is not the natural collocation in this meaning.
distractorExplanations.C: Keep discussion usually suggests continuing a discussion already in progress.
distractorExplanations.D: Carry discussion is not idiomatic here.
